summary: Adds three new debug-loop eval fixtures, each a small Python module plus pytest tests. expired-sessions: an append-only in-memory session store where get_session picks the newest row by created_at and refresh returns 404/401/200. pricing-regression: line_total and order_total with cent rounding. slow-enrichment: enrich_orders attaches customers to orders via a linear scan over a list, plus a nightly runner that times 20000x20000 records.

claims.text: get_session selects the row with the greatest created_at, ignoring version; created_at has one-second resolution per docstring.
refresh treats expires_at equal to now as expired (<=), returning status 401.
line_total computes round(unit_price*qty*(1-discount_pct/100), 2) with float arithmetic and Python round.
test_half_cent_rounds_up expects line_total(0.70,3,5)==2.00; float 1.995 rounds to 1.99 in Python, so this test fails.
index_customers returns a list of dict copies; enrich_orders scans it linearly per order, giving O(orders*customers).
run_nightly builds 20000 customers and 20000 orders and prints elapsed seconds for enrich_orders.

risks.note: Two rows with same created_at (same-second refresh) tie; max returns first, not highest version.
Float round on half-cent values (1.995) yields 1.99; test and order_total assertion likely fail.
index_customers builds a list, not a dict; nested loop does 400M comparisons on nightly input.

least_confident: Whether the pricing rounding failure and session tie-break are intentional planted bugs for the debug-loop evals or accidental; the chunk gives no eval metadata.
